topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the lecture's framing, course context, and core learning objectives regarding cancer etiology.

topics.label: Cancer as an Evolutionary Genetic Disease Driven by Intrinsic and Inherited Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe cancer development as a multi-step evolutionary process driven by clonal selection, microenvironmental factors, endogenous DNA damage, and inherited genetic predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence in Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental carcinogens, geographic variations in cancer incidence, and public perceptions contribute to understanding cancer risk.

topics.label: Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Agents
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the diverse biological and chemical pathways through which pathogens, environmental mutagens, metabolic activation, and inflammatory promoters initiate and drive tumor development.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify mutational signatures and evaluate the carcinogenic potential of agents.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides closing framing that summarises the key takeaways and reflects on everyday risk-benefit decision-making regarding carcinogens.
